Michelangelo, you said you were supposed to take first watch last night — why don't you start there? records.response_truth:

That's what almost broke us. Not the crash, not the rationing, not the rain. The uncertainty about whether everybody was actually in it together.

You're smart enough to know that. I think you knew it then too.

So keep that. Not the guilt, just the knowledge. Because you're going to be in situations for the rest of your life where you have to decide whether to trust people or go it alone and protect yourself. And now you've got a pretty clear data point on what the second option costs everybody, including you.

records.response_pred: Yeah, I get it. Stash for emergencies can be a lifesaver. How did you end up using it? Whatever the reason, glad it's there just in case.

Honestly? I'd have had that group conversation on day one instead of letting it sit. I'd also have checked in on Michelangelo more deliberately instead of just when things got visibly bad. He was giving signals the whole time, I just kept prioritizing the operational stuff over it. That was a mistake. You can't separate the people from the logistics, they're the same problem.

And I'd have been clearer earlier about what kind of group we were going to be. Like actually said it out loud — we make decisions together, we're transparent about resources, here's the deal. Instead of just assuming everybody was operating on the same social contract and then being surprised when they weren't.
